messages.subject: QTLBIM concerns
messages.body_plain:
Hello all,

I have some concerns about QTLBIM. I have a RIL population which I read in as a BC (I read on here that qtlbim will not recognize "riself").

The first concern I have is that I need to treat "RIL" as a random factor; however, when I look at the output of my qb.data() it seems to have an issue with this. It reports RILs "0 - 163"; however, it is actually 1-164.
The second issue I have concerns how qtlbim interprets "NAs". The output of my qb.data() replaces my NAs with "999.0000" (in my read.cross() statement I stated what NAs were and it read it correctly in that step). I don't know if this truly is the breeding value it interprets, but I couldn't find any documents that discussed this.
Next, when using qb.best() I get strange warnings about "1: In `levels<-`(`*tmp*`, value = c("1", "1", "2", "2", "3",  ... : duplicated levels will not be allowed in factors anymore".
Finally, when I use qb.best() the qtl that are printed out all have the exact same loci if they are on the same chromosome.  For example, when the "best pattern" suggests 2 qtl on chromosome 1 the summary statement says that both qtl are at locus 27.7390.  This is true for all chromosomes regardless of the number of qtl.
I hope that I am being clear here, I have run models using stepwiseqtl(); however, my final QTL model extremely large and I am stuck with a model selection problem.  Thus, I wanted to embark down the QTLBIM methods so I could fit qtl, qtl x e, and qtl x qtl interactions all at once.

Thanks,
Kyle

messages.subject: Discussion of model selection for genetic architecture
messages.subject_clean: Discussion of model selection for genetic architecture
messages.body_plain:
Hello again.

I would like to get some feedback on a problem I have been dealing
with. I don't expect there to be a particular solution, but I would
like to hear from different people's perspectives on model selection
issues when trying to describe the genetic architecture underlying a
trait.

Let me begin with my current approach. I decided to take a
conservative approach to discovering QTL. I have a RIL population
grown in 5 environments and I use line means as my breeding values.

1.  I analyze each of the 5 treatments separately (I will justify why
in a bit).
2.  Transform breeding values and remove outliers (this makes a huge
difference in QTL discovery)
3.  Estimate penalties using scan two with about 3000 permutations
4.  Use stepwiseqtl() with estimated penalties and about 10 qtl max
5.  Pull markers closest to discovered loci
6.  Concatenate data from each treatment into one file

First, I analyze each treatment separately because I can't use an
interactive covariate (i.e., environment) in steqwiseqtl.  In
addition, I can't control for the random effects of RIL (it is
unreasonable to assume that each RIL is independent, and I have
supported this with likelihood ratio tests in mixed models). Now here
comes a larger issue.  I can discover up to 8 QTL for a given trait
across all the environments. If I am interested in QTL,
QTLxEnvironment, QTLxQTL, and QTLxQTLxEnvironment structures, then my
full model quickly becomes unmanageable. So this is what I have done:

1.  Use glmulti() in R to select the "best" model using BIC criterion
and RIL as a random effect. However, it does NOT allow three-way
interactions. So I only build the "best" model for QTL and QTL x
Environment interactions.
2. Using that "best" model I then add QTL x QTL interactions (as
discovered by stepwiseqtl) and QTL x QTL x Environment

However, if I am interested in the genetic architecture of these
traits, and the best model doesn't include all significant
interactions then I really am getting inappropriate conclusions. For
example, for one of my traits the best model suggests QTL, QTL x QTL,
and QTL x QTL x E interactions. But it does not show QTL x E
interactions. When I add in some of these interactions they are
significant and some show very interesting patterns of effect.

I know that I am basically performing model selection on model
selection which also concerns me. The long of the short of it is, what
are appropriate ways to describe the genetic architecture when your
full model contains >15 factors and interactions?

I would really appreciate your opinions.

Thanks
Kyle

messages.subject_clean: [Rqtl-disc] scanone Error "Following phenotypes are not numeric: Column"
messages.body_plain:
At least one of the phenotype columns was interpreted as a factor rather than numeric.

If you try:

  which(!sapply(data$pheno, is.numeric))

that should tell you which columns are not numeric, which might help.

For example:

  data(hyper)
  which(!sapply(hyper$pheno, is.numeric))

Note that it's best not to use 'data' as the name of your data, since that is an important R function.

If you send me your .csv data file (privately, to kbr...@biostat.wisc.edu), I could give you more detailed help.

karl

messages.subject: physical distances
messages.body_plain:
Hello- is there a way to show physical distances on the X axis of a 1D
QTL map instead of genetic distances?
messages.body_snippet:
Hello- is there a way to show physical distances on the X axis of a 1D
QTL map instead of genetic distances?

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] physical distances
messages.body_plain:
You can use replacemap() to replace the map in scanone output with the physical map; this will use interpolation to assign physical positions to the "pseudomarker" locations.

Here's an example, using the 'hyper' data set.  These aren't physical positions, but pretend that the original map of the markers was a physical map.

data(hyper)
pmap <- pull.map(hyper) # not really physical map, but pretend

gmap <- est.map(hyper, err=0.01)
gmap <- shiftmap(gmap) # shift so each chr starts at 0 cM

hyper <- replacemap(hyper, gmap)

hyper <- calc.genoprob(hyper, step=1, err=0.01)
out <- scanone(hyper)

# replace with original map, interpolating pseudomarker positions
out.pmap <- replacemap(out, pmap)

par(mfrow=c(2,1))
plot(out, chr=c(1,4), main="Estimated map")
plot(out.pmap, chr=c(1,4), main="Original map")

karl

messages.subject_clean: Problem in indexing F2 ID numbers
messages.body_plain:
Karl:

I am trying to remove two problem F2 individuals in a selectively genotyped mapping populations (p1076) using the below commands.
There are 44 genotyped individuals (22 high protein + 22 low protein) in the phenotyped population of 188 F2 individuals.
The problem is that after I remove these two F2s from the p1076 object using the commands below, the later assignment comments do not work.
I know that I could simply remove the individuals from the csv file, but I would prefer to keep that csv file intact as I attempt various error checks.

Below was excerpted from my R/qtl input file after reading in the csv file into a p1076 object:

#  Use below commands to drop TWO "problem" individual F2s.

temp1 <- p1076[ , "-160"]
temp2 <- temp1[ , "-163"]
p1076 <- temp2

#  The below assignment commands create two subsets of the P1076 population Selectively Genotyped F2 ID#s.
#  These were created so that I could look at the plot.geno output for the 44 genotypes in two uncrowded (22 each) graphs:

px1076 <- c(1,2,4,5,6,7,10,21,26,27,29,31,32,47,49,57,61,68,71,87,92,93)
py1076 <- c(95,104,105,109,111,114,120,123,124,125,126,129,132,136,156,157,160,163,165,169,171,174)

plot.geno(p1076, chr=c(1), ind=c(px1076), cutoff=5, min.sep=2)
mtext("White=AA Grey=AB Black=BB  BlueX=XO  RedBox=GenoError?", side=3, line=1, las=1)
mtext("P1076 Marker", side=1, line=2, las=1)
plot.geno(p1076, chr=c(1), ind=c(py1076), cutoff=5, min.sep=2)
mtext("White=AA Grey=AB Black=BB  BlueX=XO  RedBox=GenoError?", side=3, line=1, las=1)
mtext("P1076 Marker", side=1, line=2, las=1)

The above plot.geno graphs do not provide correct output apparently (I think) because the F2 ID# is no longer correctly maintained (in R/qtl p1076) after I drop the two individuals.
Is this a bug? Or is there a better (command) means of dropping the two individuals that cause this problem.  Any suggestions?

I am including the p1076.csv file for your perusal.  The F2 ID# in the first row is not contiguous (some F2 plants were lost), but the F2 plant derived F3 seed progeny row number is contiguous from 1-188 (at least before dropping the two above individuals).

- Jim

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Problem in indexing F2 ID numbers
messages.subject_clean: [Rqtl-disc] Problem in indexing F2 ID numbers
messages.body_plain:
Dear Jim,

I think it's working okay; it's just the IDs are interpreted differently if you give numbers versus if you give character strings.

As numbers, ind=px1076 in calls to plot.geno will take the first, second, 4th, 5th, ..., 93rd, individuals.
As character strings ind=as.character(px1076) in calls to plot.geno will look for those individual IDs in the "ID" column in the data set.

Consider the different result you get when you do the following:

plot.geno(p1076, chr=c(1), ind=as.character(px1076), cutoff=5, min.sep=2)

mtext("White=AA Grey=AB Black=BB  BlueX=XO  RedBox=GenoError?", side=3, line=1, las=1)
mtext("P1076 Marker", side=1, line=2, las=1)

plot.geno(p1076, chr=c(1), ind=as.character(py1076), cutoff=5, min.sep=2)

mtext("White=AA Grey=AB Black=BB  BlueX=XO  RedBox=GenoError?", side=3, line=1, las=1)
mtext("P1076 Marker", side=1, line=2, las=1)

In particular, you get the warning messages:

 In subset.cross(cross, ind = ind) : Individuals not found: 4 29 68 92
 In subset.cross(cross, ind = ind) : Individuals not found: 124 160 163

karl
